reasons_add: Sibawayh further traces wāw-to-yāʾ changes to kasra and a following alif or yāʾ-like sound in verbal nouns and plurals, including qiyām, siyāṭ, thiyāb and riyāḍ; a substituted yāʾ can persist in the plural. He distinguishes retained original wāw in sound-verb nouns, certain plurals, fuʿūl, augmented patterns and forms without the conditioning kasra; wāw after ḍamma may instead be hamzated. He marks thawra/thīra as nonproductive. Some speakers extend the fiʿl analogy irregularly to fiʿlān and fuʿlā.
Al-Itqān reports Ibn al-Labbān's reading of seeking God's face as sincerity of intention, comparing feeding others for God's sake.

Saʿd's report in Ibn Mājah names himself, Ibn Masʿūd, Suhayb, ʿAmmār, al-Miqdād and Bilāl as the six believers Quraysh wanted expelled; his report in Muslim explicitly names himself, Ibn Masʿūd and Bilāl among six.
